proposals.expected_signal: Higher frozen full-sort NDCG@10 from reducing head-item domination while preserving collaborative propagation signal.
proposals.failure_mode: If popularity bias is not the main bottleneck, degree tempering will weaken useful high-frequency edges and lower ranking quality across all users.
proposals.hypothesis: Apply edge normalization with a tunable degree-temperature during light graph propagation so high-degree users/items contribute less aggressively than in standard symmetric normalization, improving long-tail discrimination.

proposals.expected_signal: NDCG@10 gain if learned message transforms can separate helpful neighbor evidence from noisy interactions better than fixed propagation.
proposals.failure_mode: If ML-1M is too small for the extra capacity, the transform layers will overfit or destabilize training and underperform simpler graph models.
proposals.hypothesis: Use a graph recommender with lightweight per-edge message transforms and residual gating so each hop can adaptively filter or amplify neighbor information instead of treating all propagated embeddings linearly.

proposals.expected_signal: If graph propagation is not essential under the fixed protocol, a debiased MF baseline may recover competitive NDCG@10 with lower complexity and clearer attribution.
proposals.failure_mode: If higher-order connectivity is necessary for top-10 ranking, the latent factor model will remain structurally capped and miss graph-based gains.
proposals.hypothesis: Keep a latent-factor model but reweight pairwise ranking updates by item popularity buckets so the optimizer spends less capacity reinforcing already-easy popular negatives and more on informative medium/long-tail distinctions.

proposals.expected_signal: Improved NDCG@10 if a contrastive auxiliary stabilizes representation geometry and makes user/item embeddings more invariant to sparse edge perturbations.
proposals.failure_mode: If the auxiliary loss dominates or the augmentations are too destructive, the model will optimize invariance at the expense of ranking fidelity and hurt top-k metrics.
proposals.hypothesis: Train a light propagation backbone with the standard ranking loss plus a contrastive auxiliary between two stochastic graph views created by mild edge dropout, encouraging consistent embeddings while preserving the unchanged evaluation protocol.
